'''Steel Cross''' is a village in the north-east of [[Crowborough]], in the [[Wealden District|Wealden]] district, in the county of [[East Sussex]], [[England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wealden.gov.uk/UploadedFiles/Figure14_1.pdf|publisher=[[Wealden  District Council]]|work=Wealden Local Plan|title=Figure 14.1 {{!}} Land at Steel Cross|date=December 2005|access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>

== Geography ==
Steel Cross is located in the northern region of East Sussex, England. It is in the north-east of Crowborough and is south-west of [[Royal Tunbridge Wells|Tunbridge Wells]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Election Maps |url=https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/election-maps/gb/index.html |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk}}</ref> The village is half-way in the [[Jarvis Brook]] ward.<ref>{{Cite web |title=City Population: Check for Humans |url=https://www.citypopulation.de/checkhuman.html?url=%2Fen%2Fuk%2Fsoutheastengland%2Fwards%2Fwealden%2FE05011629__crowborough_jarvis_brook%2F |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=www.citypopulation.de}}</ref>

== Transport ==
The main road in Steel Cross is the [[A26 road|A26]] which runs north-east to [[Maidstone]] and south to [[Newhaven, East Sussex|Newhaven]]. The [[Brighton & Hove (bus company)#The Regency Route|29 Regency Route]] bus runs through the centre of the village.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regency 29 - Brighton - Tunbridge Wells and Heathfield |url=https://www.buses.co.uk/services/BH/29 |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=www.buses.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

== Sport and leisure ==
Steel Cross is home to Crowborough Rugby Football Club<ref>{{Cite web|title=Steel Cross Venue Hire|url=https://www.crowboroughrugby.com/a/steel-cross-venue-hire-42606.html|website=www.crowboroughrugby.com|access-date=2026-01-31}}</ref> and a 9 hole Par 35 Golf Course.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Parkfield Golf Club |url=https://www.parkfieldgolf.co.uk/ |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=www.parkfieldgolf.co.uk}}</ref>

== History ==
The earliest documented representations of Steel Cross are in 1724 as a part of the 1 inch to 1 mile map of [[Sussex]] produced in 1724 by Richard Budgen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Weald - Property history, bibliography and topography |url=https://theweald.org/P3.asp?PId=Cr.SteelX |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=theweald.org}}</ref> Historical maps show the road network and scattered buildings that formed the centre of the [[Hamlet (place)|hamlet]], reflecting its origins as an agricultural locality within the High Weald landscape.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Weald - Property history, bibliography and topography |url=https://theweald.org/P3.asp?PId=Cr.SteelX |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=theweald.org}}</ref> 

Throughout the 20th century, Steel Cross remained a small, predominantly residential and agricultural community within the Crowborough Civil parish. Its location along the [[A26 road|A26]] meant that it served local travellers and residents, with amenities such as a village post office historically serving the immediate area.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Poundfield in Crowborough {{!}} Royal Mail Group Ltd |url=https://www.royalmail.com/services-near-you/post-office/poundfield-tn6-2bh}}</ref>

There used to be a school named "Steel Cross National School" in Steel Cross<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Weald - Maps |url=https://theweald.org/m00.asp?PicIdto=35150004 |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=theweald.org}}</ref> which was built in 1865 opened in 1866 and closed just before the [[World War II|2nd World War]]. The school was funded by the Goldsmith family and the average attendance was 100 children. On the [[gable]] of the building there is a Goldmith's emblem.<ref>https://www.facebook.com/groups/520522518060261/posts/6929559533823162/</ref>
